m:acropoli: Ticket €30 all year, for a single entry with a 2-hour time slot: buy it online at hhticket.gr (up to 60 days ahead; in summer book 1–3 weeks in advance) and there are no skip-the-line tickets. The combined ticket for several sites was scrapped in 2025: each site has its own. Until 31 October hours are 8am–7:30pm (last entry 7pm), from November 8am–5pm (last entry 4:30pm). Closed on 1 January, 25 March, 1 May, Greek Easter, 25 and 26 December. Free on 28 October (with booking). Wear shoes with non-slip soles: the marble is polished. Data from guides, not checked on the Ministry website: to be confirmed.
m:museoac: Ticket €20 all year (reduced €10). Until 31 October open every day 8am–8pm, Fridays until 10pm; from November Monday–Thursday 9am–5pm, Friday 9am–10pm, Saturday and Sunday 9am–8pm. Closed on 1 January, 1 May, Greek Easter and 25 and 26 December. Buy online on the museum website (up to 30 days ahead). Free on 28 October. Friday evening is the best time, with the Acropolis lit up outside the windows (from guides, to be confirmed).
m:plaka: Free to walk around. The main streets (Adrianou, Kydathineon) have tourist restaurants and souvenir shops: to eat, it's better to move to the side streets. For Anafiotika, go up the steps from Stratonos or Theorias.
m:agora: Ticket €20 (includes the museum in the Stoa of Attalos). Until 31 October 8am–8pm, from November 8am–5pm; last entry 20 minutes before closing. One of the entrances (Adrianou street) appears to be closed for works: use the Apostolou Pavlou entrance, near Thissio. Prices and hours from secondary guides, to be confirmed.
m:romana: Roman Agora €10, Hadrian's Library €10 (two separate tickets). Until 31 October 8am–8pm; from November hours are shorter (8am–5pm for the Roman Agora; Hadrian's Library appears to close at 3pm). From the street you can already see the Tower of the Winds and part of the Library. From guides, to be confirmed.
m:zeus: Ticket €20 (from guides). Until 31 October from 8am until sunset, in winter 8am–3pm. The arch and the columns are also clearly visible from outside, for free, from Amalias avenue. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
m:stadio: Ticket €12 with an audio guide in 11 languages (from athenstourism.org, to be confirmed as other sources give a higher price). Open every day 8am–7pm from March to October, 8am–5pm from November to February. Closed on 1 January, 1 May, Greek Easter and 25 December. Tickets are only sold at the stadium ticket office.
m:syntagma: Free. The simple changing of the guard is every hour, on the hour, and takes a few minutes; the full ceremonial parade with the band and full uniforms is on Sundays at 11am and lasts about twenty minutes. There are often demonstrations and marches in the square: if they're very crowded, take another route.
m:museoarch: Ticket €20 all year according to two guides (another source gives €12 in summer and €6 in winter: to be confirmed). Until 31 October Tuesday–Sunday 8:30am–8pm, Monday 1–8pm; from November Tuesday–Sunday 8:30am–4pm, Monday 1–5pm. Closed on 1 January, 25 March, 1 May, Greek Easter and 25 and 26 December. Free on 28 October.
m:filopappo: Free, always open. The climb takes 15–20 minutes on stony, partly dirt paths: wear comfortable shoes. Walk from Akropoli stop (metro line 2) or from Thissio. It's very busy at sunset.
m:licabetto: Free on foot (about 20 minutes of steep climbing from Kolonaki, on steps and a path). You can also take the funicular from the base on Aristippou street (about €7 one way, €10 return; every 30 minutes from 9am to 2:30am, 2023 data, to be confirmed). Crowded at sunset.
vd:yiasemi: A small café with a jasmine garden in the upper streets of Plaka, for breakfast, brunch and Greek coffee. You eat outdoors in the shade, a few minutes from the climb to the Acropolis.
vp:yiasemi: Breakfast or brunch around €5–12 (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:tristrato: A café on a pedestrian street in Plaka where Greek coffee arrives in a copper pot; with your coffee there's baklava and other syrup pastries.
vp:tristrato: A Greek coffee with a pastry costs €5–10 (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:dianthos: A quality coffee and pastry counter a few steps from Monastiraki square, for an espresso or an iced Greek coffee before heading into the Agora.
vp:dianthos: A coffee with a pastry around €4–8 (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:klepsidra: A café in a flowery courtyard below the Tower of the Winds, with a view of the Acropolis: iced coffee, cakes and snacks for a break between stops.
vp:klepsidra: A coffee with a snack is around €5–10 (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:bairaktaris: The souvlaki tavern on Monastiraki square, open since 1879: gyros and souvlaki in pita, or served at the table with chips, salad and bread. A quick meal in a busy, simple place, open late (until 2am).
vp:bairaktaris: A pita with meat costs about €4; a plate at the table €8–15 (from guides). Hours from athenspotlighted.gr: 9am–2am every day, to be confirmed.
vd:kostas: A small kiosk from 1950 on Agia Irini square: few seats, grilled meat and pita made to order. It closes when the meat runs out, usually in the early afternoon.
vp:kostas: A pita costs about €3.50 (from guides), cash only. Closed at weekends according to one listing (another says Sundays only): to be confirmed.
vd:diporto: A tavern with no sign in a basement near the central market: there's no menu, you eat whatever there is at shared tables, with house wine drawn from the barrel. A genuine place, for those not in a hurry.
vp:diporto: Lunch is around €12–18 per person (from guides), cash only, no bookings. Open for lunch Monday to Saturday, closed Sunday (from an online listing, to be confirmed).
vd:karamanlidika: A deli-tavern a short walk from the central market, specialising in cured meats and cheeses from northern Greece (pastourma, sausages, graviera) and Anatolian dishes. Eat at the counter or at tables.
vp:karamanlidika: A meal with cold cuts, cheeses and a glass of wine is around €25–35 (from guides). Hours from an online listing (Monday–Saturday noon–midnight, Sunday noon–6pm): to be confirmed.
vd:platanos: One of the oldest taverns in Plaka, with tables under a plane tree in a little square: oven-baked lamb (kleftiko), gigantes beans, stewed octopus and simple salads.
vp:platanos: A meal with a main course is around €18–30 (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:kafeneio: A place in the style of a traditional coffee house in the upper lanes of Plaka, with small plates to share and house wine from the barrel. Sometimes there's live music in the evening.
vp:kafeneio: You eat for about €15–22 per person (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:diogenis: A small neighbourhood tavern behind Plaka's main street, with home cooking: moussaka, gemista (stuffed vegetables) and wine from the barrel.
vp:diogenis: You eat for about €15–22 per person (from guides). Hours not checked: to be confirmed.
cd:benaki: Seven thousand years of Greek art, from prehistory to the 20th century, in a neoclassical villa.
cd:ciclatico: Marble Cycladic idols and a wing of ancient Greek art.
cd:ceramico: The ancient cemetery and potters' quarter, with a small museum.
cd:licafun: The funicular that climbs to the chapel at the top of the hill.
cd:bizantino: Icons, mosaics and textiles from the Byzantine Empire, in a building with a garden.
cd:emst: A former brewery with Greek and international art.
cd:numismatico: Coins from antiquity, in Heinrich Schliemann's neoclassical house.
cd:kerameikosm: Ceramics, textiles and objects from the Islamic world.
